factors.factor: Command tooling lacked safeguards (input validation, scope limits, confirmation of resolved server count) against an incorrectly entered parameter, so a single incorrect input could remove far more servers than intended and the playbook did not catch the overly broad removal before it reached production capacity
factors.evidence: "One of the inputs to the command was entered incorrectly and a larger set of servers was removed than intended." | "an authorized S3 team member using an established playbook executed a command which was intended to remove a small number of servers"

factors.factor: Servers supporting multiple critical subsystems (index and placement) were coupled to a single removal operation, so the scope of impact exceeded the scope of the intended change
factors.evidence: "The servers that were removed supported two other S3 subsystems."

factors.factor: Critical subsystems required full restarts rather than being able to recover incrementally after capacity loss, extending the outage
factors.evidence: "Removing a significant portion of the capacity caused each of these systems to require a full restart."

factors.factor: Restart and metadata integrity safety checks were slower than expected, prolonging recovery time
factors.evidence: "The process of restarting these services and running the necessary safety checks to validate the integrity of the metadata took longer than expected."

factors.factor: Strong dependency of the service health dashboard administration console on S3 prevented status updates to customers during the outage
factors.evidence: "the team was unable to update the individual services' status on the AWS Service Health Dashboard (SHD) because of a dependency the SHD administration console has on Amazon S3."

factors.factor: Heavy reliance on S3 by other AWS services in the region propagated the impact to EC2, EBS, Lambda, and the S3 console
factors.evidence: "Other AWS services in the US-EAST-1 Region that rely on S3 for storage, including the S3 console, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) new instance launches, Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes (when data was needed from a S3 snapshot), and AWS Lambda were also impacted"

factors.factor: Accumulated backlogs in dependent services extended recovery after S3 was restored
factors.evidence: "Some of these services had accumulated a backlog of work during the S3 disruption and required additional time to fully recover."

action_items.action: Add input validation and confirmation safeguards to the capacity-removal command, such as requiring explicit confirmation of the resolved server count and blocking removals that exceed a defined threshold without an additional approval step.
Revise the capacity-removal playbook to require a dry-run that lists the exact servers affected and verifies that none support critical index or placement subsystems before execution.
Decouple the servers supporting the index and placement subsystems from the servers used by the billing subsystem so that a single removal operation cannot affect multiple critical subsystems.
Modify the index and placement subsystems to support incremental recovery from partial capacity loss instead of requiring full restarts.
action_items.owner_role: S3 index and placement subsystem teams

action_items.action: Optimize the restart and metadata integrity safety checks, and establish measured recovery time targets for each critical subsystem, validated through regular restart testing.
Remove the dependency of the Service Health Dashboard administration console on S3 by hosting it in a separate, independently available infrastructure.
Map and reduce intra-region dependencies on S3 for control-plane functions in EC2, EBS, Lambda, and the S3 console, and document fallback behavior for each.
Add alerting on rapid capacity loss within S3 subsystems so that the on-call rotation is paged before the loss causes service unavailability.
Establish backlog-draining procedures and rate-limiting for dependent services so they recover in a controlled manner after an upstream dependency is restored.
